title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Pacifica Bank
next_steps: Redwood to upload SOC 2 Type II report and most recent pen-test artifacts to secure share (Jordan) - target 2026-12-04
Pacifica InfoSec to send completed SIG PDF back with high-priority questions highlighted (Priya) - target 2026-12-07
Schedule deep-dive on KMS/BYOK and network setup with Pacifica Cloud team (Sofia + Tom) - calendar invite by 2026-12-02
Redwood to provide architecture diagram and steps for Private deployment evidence (Marcus) - target 2026-12-06
action_items: Jordan Lee (Redwood): Share SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, and ISO cert copy via secure link - due 2026-12-04
Marcus Nguyen (Redwood): Provide KMS key policy example and HSM/BYOK options doc - due 2026-12-06
Sofia Patel (Redwood): Send diagram of VPC peering/private deployment network flow and sample audit-log retention screenshots - due 2026-12-06
Priya Shah (Pacifica): Return SIG with flagged items and any evidence requests prioritized - due 2026-12-07
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-30 | Start: 15:00 PST | Duration: 55 minutes | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Sofia Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Nguyen (Redwood SecEng); Angela Ramos (Pacifica InfoSec), Tom Becker (Pacifica Cloud), Priya Shah (Pacifica Vendor Risk), David O'Connor (Pacifica Legal)
summary: Walkthrough of Pacifica Bank SIG/CAIQ questionnaire. Focus on SOC 2 / ISO evidence, RBAC & SSO integration approach (SAML/SCIM), audit logging and retention, data residency options (US-only), encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/BYOK, and evidence delivery channels. Redwood outlined hosted vs private deployment controls and provided tentative timeline to deliver artifacts.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we have about 55 minutes, we'll go section by section through the SIG - I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood.
[00:12] Angela Ramos: Hi Jordan, thanks. We're primarily looking for the SOC2 evidence and clarifications on KMS and data residency.
[00:20] Sofia Patel: Hey all, Sofia here on the SE side, I'll run the technical bits - network, encryption, SSO.
[00:28] Tom Becker: Quick note, Pacifca's cloud team will need to know whether Private deployment requires air-gapped hardware or can be VPC-peered into our AWS account.
[00:40] Jordan Lee: Good point. We'll mark that - Redwood Private supports both VPC peering and on-prem packages; we can outline options.
[00:50] [00:50] Marcus Nguyen: From a security evidence POV, we typically provide SOC 2 Type II, pen test report redacted, and an ISO 27001 certificate if requested. For KMS, we support AWS KMS, customer-managed keys (BYOK), and HSM-backed options.
[01:10] Priya Shah: For SIG question 3.4 (encryption at rest) - do you use AES-256, and can customers manage keys? We need exact language for our risk team.
[01:22] Sofia Patel: Yes, AES-256 for rest, TLS1.2+ for transit. BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated, hosted has KMS integration with customer-managed keys on request - we'll include key rotation details.
[01:36] David O'Connor: Are you able to provide key custody documentation and a sample KMS policy? Our legal needs to see contract language for key access.
[01:45] Marcus Nguyen: Absolutely, we'll provide a sample key policy and notes on access controls - Redwood personnel do not have direct access to customer keys when BYOK is enabled; we can include an appendix.
[02:00] [02:00] Tom Becker: On RBAC and SSO, can you confirm SAML + SCIM provisioning, and role hierarchy? We need SCIM sync to our Azure AD.
[02:12] Sofia Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync. Roles are mapped by group claims; fine-grained RBAC controls are available in Private and Dedicated, hosted supports org-level roles and service roles.
[02:30] Angela Ramos: Audit logs - how long do you retain logs by default, and can we export them to our SIEM?
[02:40] Marcus Nguyen: Default retention is 90 days in hosted, configurable up to 365 days for Dedicated/Private. Logs can be forwarded via secure syslog or delivered to customer S3/GCS buckets; integration with SIEM is supported.
[02:58] [03:00] Priya Shah: For the SIG, question about incident response and breach notification - what's your SLA to notify customers?
[03:10] Jordan Lee: Our incident response policy commits to notification within 72 hours for confirmed incidents, and critical incidents have an escalation path; we'll attach the IR playbook summary.
[03:22] Tom Becker: Data residency, we require US-only processing and storage for this contract. Can Redwood guarantee that?
[03:30] Sofia Patel: Yes, we can guarantee region restrictions - hosted can be pinned to US regions, Dedicated and Private obviously host in your desired region or on-prem. We'll note how to configure region policies.
[03:45] [03:45] Angela Ramos: Regarding SIG evidence delivery - is there a secure portal or SFTP for sensitive docs? We can't accept public links.
[03:55] Jordan Lee: We'll use a secure share - we can upload into your vendor portal or provide time-limited SSO-protected links, or use secure SFTP depending on your preference.
[04:10] [04:10] Priya Shah: A couple of SIG items are high priority: 1) SOC 2 report, 2) pen test exec summary, 3) encryption key custody.
[04:20] Marcus Nguyen: We'll prioritize those. For pen test, we provide redacted reports plus a summary of findings and mitigations; full reports go through an NDA if needed.
[04:32] [04:32] David O'Connor: Can you confirm third-party subprocessor list and whether any subprocessors have access to decrypted data?
[04:42] Sofia Patel: Subprocessors are documented; most subprocessors are cloud infra providers and observability partners. Decrypted data access is restricted - only necessary service components have access and it's covered by our contracts; we'll include the current subprocessors list.
[04:58] [05:00] Tom Becker: For network isolation in Private deployment, what are the typical customer responsibilities vs Redwood-managed parts?
[05:10] Sofia Patel: We'll deliver a responsibilities matrix; generally, customer controls VPC, peering, and routing rules; Redwood manages the app layer and instance configuration, but we can run in your account if required.
[05:24] Angela Ramos: Does Redwood support MFA for admin users and enforced password policies?
[05:30] Marcus Nguyen: Yes MFA required for all admin roles, password policies configurable, and session timeout policies available.
[05:40] [05:40] Priya Shah: SIG has an item about continuous monitoring - do you provide CV scanning, SAST/DAST?
[05:50] Sofia Patel: We have internal CI/CD checks, dependency scanning, SAST for our codebase and scheduled pen tests annually, and we can provide summaries of those programs.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: Quick note - a common question we see is latency vs encryption tradeoffs in Dedicated vs Hosted; not sure if you want us to add performance numbers to the SIG response.
[06:14] Tom Becker: Performance numbers would help, yes. We have a perf gate for some latency-sensitive flows.
[06:22] Sofia Patel: We'll annotate the SIG with recommended instance types and an expected p50/p95 latency for common request sizes.
[06:35] [06:35] Angela Ramos: A few SIG questions are about change management and patching cadence, what do you typically provide?
[06:44] Marcus Nguyen: We have a monthly patch cycle for noncritical patches and emergency patching for critical CVEs; we'll attach our change control policy and SRM notes.
[06:58] [07:00] Priya Shah: Regarding audit logs again - do logs include admin actions, API calls, and token issuance? We need to show proof for a sample period.
[07:10] Sofia Patel: Yes, audit logs include user admin actions, API calls, and auth events. We'll provide example log snippets and a schema.
[07:22] David O'Connor: For legal, we need to understand liability carve-outs for subprocessors and encryption failures. Can you indicate standard contract language?
[07:34] Jordan Lee: We can share our standard DPA and subprocessor terms; we also offer enterprise contract addenda for higher assurance. We'll flag legal to share standard clauses.
[07:50] [07:50] Tom Becker: Back to KMS - if we choose BYOK in hosted, what's the integration flow and who rotates keys?
[08:00] Marcus Nguyen: For hosted BYOK we integrate via your AWS KMS or external HSM. Rotation can be customer-managed or automated with a rotation schedule; we'll provide step-by-step and a sample KMS policy.
[08:12] Priya Shah: Does Redwood ever hold plaintext for support troubleshooting?
[08:20] Sofia Patel: No - support access is limited and audited; plaintext access requires explicit customer consent and is rare; we record any such access in audit logs.
[08:35] [08:35] Angela Ramos: For SIG CAIQ items about secure disposal and data deletion - what's your retention and deletion approach?
[08:45] Marcus Nguyen: Data retention varies by product and plan; we default to token retention for X days but can implement retention TTLs and immediate deletion for Private deployments; we'll include deletion proof examples.
[09:00] Jordan Lee: We'll note specific SIG answers for data lifecycle.
[09:08] [09:08] Priya Shah: A tricky SIG item is about background checks for privileged operators - do you perform those?
[09:16] Marcus Nguyen: For staff with privileged access we do background checks; details vary by role but we'll provide the HR policy summary.
[09:30] [09:30] Tom Becker: Any SOC bridge letters or interim reports available if the latest SOC2 isn't aligned with our timeline?
[09:40] Jordan Lee: We can provide a bridge letter and state the audit period; will include timeline for next audit if helpful.
[09:50] [09:50] Angela Ramos: Can you show an example of your audit log retention configuration for 365 days in Dedicated?
[09:58] Sofia Patel: Yes, we'll provide screenshots and config snippets.
[10:05] [10:05] Priya Shah: We sometimes ask for live demos of security controls - is that possible under NDA?
[10:12] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can arrange a gated demo or live walkthrough with security masking under NDA.
[10:20] [10:20] Marcus Nguyen: One more note - subprocessors list includes cloud provider, monitoring provider, and a model-serving partner; we'll mark which handle encrypted data and which only handle telemetry.
[10:35] Tom Becker: Regarding the SIG question on service availability and backups - what's the RTO/RPO for Dedicated vs Private?
[10:45] Sofia Patel: Dedicated targets SLA-backed uptime and recovery strategies; Private depends on customer infra but we provide guidance. We'll put RTO/RPO examples in the SIG responses.
[11:00] [11:00] David O'Connor: Ok, legal will review the redlines after we receive the DPA and SOC report.
[11:08] Jordan Lee: Great. To close out, we'll summarize the prioritized evidence list and action items in an email.
[11:18] [11:18] Angela Ramos: Thanks, this was helpful.
[11:22] Priya Shah: We'll get the SIG back to you with flags.
[11:28] Jordan Lee: Perfect - thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and the calendar invite for the KMS deep-dive.
[11:35] [11:35] Meeting end.
